content.overview: Section 14 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 lists the contracts which cannot be specifically enforced. After the 2018 amendment they are: a contract of which a party has obtained substituted performance under section 20; a contract whose performance involves a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; a contract so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and a contract which is in its nature determinable. These are bars to section 10. They are not a general discretion to refuse every hard contract.
content.study: Use section 14 only for one of the four enacted classes. A contract that is merely inconvenient is not in the list. If substituted performance has been taken, stop.

learningObjectives: Keep unlisted hardship out of the section.
enhancement.definition: Section 14 is the list of contracts that cannot be specifically enforced: substituted performance, unsupervised continuous duty, personal qualifications, and a determinable contract.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 10 yields only to the enacted bars. A contract outside section 14 is not refused merely because performance is burdensome.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Specific Relief Act, 1963, section 14, as amended in 2018. Section 20 is the substituted-performance section.
essentialIngredients: Substituted performance already obtained under section 20, or
Continuous duty the court cannot supervise
Performance dependent on personal qualifications so that material terms cannot be enforced
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Clause (a) is the election in section 20. Once the promisee has obtained substituted performance, the contract cannot be specifically enforced. Clause (b) is continuous performance that the court cannot supervise, not every contract that takes time. Clause (c) is dependence on personal qualifications, such as a contract of personal service whose material terms the court cannot enforce. Clause (d) is a contract determinable in its nature, meaning the defendant can bring it to an end under its terms. The section does not add a fifth bar of inadequate consideration or hardship. Those older grounds are not restated as section 14.
examples: The owner has had the building completed by another contractor after the section 20 notice. Clause (a) bars specific performance.
A contract to paint a portrait depends on personal qualifications. Clause (c) is the bar.
A fixed sale of identified land is not determinable and needs no continuous supervision. Section 14 does not list it.
enhancement.problemApplication: Place the contract in one of the four clauses or accept that section 14 does not bar it. Then check section 16.
distinctions: Section 14 contract bar vs section 16 plaintiff bar
Substituted performance vs a mere claim for damages
Continuous duty the court cannot supervise vs a one-time conveyance
Determinable contract vs a contract the defendant regrets
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Ready-and-willing and adequate-relief readings remain on the case-law gate.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Section 14 bars specific performance of four classes: substituted performance, unsupervised continuous duty, personal qualifications, and a determinable contract.

keyTakeaways: An unsupervised continuous duty is not enforceable.
Personal qualifications can bar enforcement of material terms.
A determinable contract is not specifically enforced.
Hardship is not a fifth section 14 bar.

verification.note: Section 14 as amended. No case ratio on determinable contracts.
